column60: I had to take my time with reading the article in order to fully understand it. Truthfully, I am not terribly familiar with the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, but I know that there are many innocent people who are caught in the middle of it. When reading over the article, I had to go back and forth between paragraphs multiple times to ensure that I wasn't misinterpreting anything. I wanted to see if the language and tone was consistent throughout, and whether any specific techniques were utilized to obscure propaganda and/or political bias. My findings led me to believe that the author of the article most certainly has a negative outlook towards Ukraine; this is evident by the first sentence of the article itself. More specifically, the lack of quotation marks for something that is evidently a quote and not a pure fact. For anyone unfamiliar with political bias, there's a high chance that they'll misinterpret certain sections of the article as the outright truth. While the article uses language that is much more subdued than the first piece, the bias is still there in the overall direction and framing, even if the language isn't necessarily hostile. It's thinly-veiled accusations backed by opinions from Russia's side; it does not bother to consider Ukraine whatsoever, and instead antagonizes them while masquerading as something that might be mistaken as a trustworthy, politically-neutral piece, just because it quotes certain political figures. However, it's always important to bear in mind that quotes of speculation do not necessarily stand for anything substantial or factual (with the exception of negating purely personal affairs unrelated to other parties in conflict, e.g. dissuasion of rumours), especially when it comes to politics.
column68: There are multiple instances where the framing of the article steers into propaganda, even if it's more subtle than the first article. It has mostly to do with the lack of quotation marks (to mislead readers), primarily focusing on giving a vocal platform to those who oppose Ukraine, and generally insinuating that Ukraine is the sole troublemaker in this entire ordeal. The article serves to sway the reader's opinion into favouring Russia and letting them believe that Ukraine is the only one refusing to negotiate, and thus the only prolonging the conflict. They never question why Ukraine may be unwilling to negotiate, insinuating that they simply do not wish to take accountability even if Russia is supposedly willing to negotiate something for peace.
